title: introduce-kv-tessellator-and-late-writeback-with-spillback-smoother
author: Maya Chen
description:
Context and motivation: The KV cache is showing higher-than-expected fragmentation under mixed tenant workloads and bursty loads that trigger large spill waves. Existing evictors reduce residency but often produce large contiguous spill bursts that overload the paging pipeline and cause tail-latency regressions for interactive tenants. This PR introduces two coordinated subsystems: a lightweight memory tessellator (re-segments large sparse extents into small, defragmentation-friendly tiles) and a late-writeback/soft-spillback smoother (staggers spill I/O and reorders writeback to minimize peak throughput). Together they reduce fragmentation score, smooth spillback traffic, and keep hot prefixes resident for continuous-batching workloads.

Design summary: 1) Tessellator: a background sampler that scans large KV segments and emits small 'tiles' (configurable: default 4KB-64KB) for preferential retention and compact-on-rewrite. The tessellator produces a fragmentation score per segment using a stochastic histogram; scores feed into the evictor priority queue so we bias against evicting tiles that reduce downstream KV lookups. Tessellator is non-blocking and restart-safe (state stored in per-tenant checkpoints).

2) Late-writeback & Spillback smoother: when eviction decides to spill, we attach spill candidates to a smoothing window controlled by an adaptive leaky-bucket. The window reshapes output into smaller, more frequent batches rather than large coalesced writes. A backpressure hook integrates with the scheduler so that when paging IO saturates, the smoother increases in-memory demotion and defers low-priority tiles.

3) Integration with continuous batching: the tessellator marks tiles as 'batch-friendly' when their access patterns indicate frequent prefix reuse. The request router and batcher use this hint to preferentially colocate requests to nodes with those tiles cached, increasing per-batch cache hit-rate.

What changed (high level files): - src/kv/cache/tessellator.cpp (new) - include/kv/tessellator.h (new) - src/kv/evictor/spill_smoother.cpp (new) - src/kv/evictor/evictor_integration.cpp (modifications to accept tile-priority hints) - tests/kv/tessellator_test.cpp (unit + microbench) - tests/kv/spill_smoother_integration_test.cpp - docs/ops/kv-memory-tuning.md (new section + examples) - examples/benchmarks/fragbench.yaml (added scenario)

Commits (summary): - Add tessellator core loop, sampling heuristics and checkpointing (Maya Chen) - Implement spillback smoother and leaky-bucket controller (Maya Chen) - Wire tile-priority into evictor and scheduler hooks (Ben Rodriguez) - Add unit and integration tests + basic perf bench (Priya Nair) - Docs and ops notes; tuning defaults (Liam O'Connor)

Checklist (manual & automated): - [x] Unit tests for tessellator sampling and checkpointing - [x] Integration test for spill smoothing under synthetic IO saturation - [x] Microbenchmark comparing fragmentation score before/after - [x] Docs describing tuning knobs and safety defaults - [x] Feature gated behind runtime flag (kv.tessellator_enabled = false by default for canary rollout)

Testing and validation: Local microbenchmarks on fragbench scenario show a 28% reduction in measured fragmentation score and a 15% reduction in 99th-percentile tail latency under bursty writes on a 4-tenant mixed workload. End-to-end CI included unit tests and an integration scenario that simulates sustained spillback. A flaky paging test failed on first CI run due to timing; rerun passed and full CI is green.

Review conversation (high level): - Priya: "Nice work. Can we avoid additional lock contention in the tessellator when checkpoints are emitted?"  Author reply: "Tessellator uses per-tenant RCU-style buffers; checkpointing is off the hot path and emits only delta positions to the checkpoint store. I added a unit test that asserts locking time < 200us on 8-thread stress." - Ben: "Integration looks clean but rebalancer may starve low-priority tenants if smoothing defers too aggressively."  Author reply: "Added adaptive priority decay and a tenant-sla knob; default keeps fairness unchanged. See tests/spill_smoother_integration_test for enforcement." - Liam: "Docs are essential here for on-call tuning — good that you added examples."  Author reply: "Expanded ops doc with recommended defaults and a rollback recipe."

CI: Initial run - paging_flaky_test timed out (flake) -> rerun -> all checks passed. Summaries: unit (pass), integration (pass), perf-bench (pass, CI-simulated), lint (pass), docs-build (pass).

Rollback and safety: Feature is behind kv.tessellator_enabled flag and the smoother behind kv.spill_smoother_enabled. Rolling back is safe by toggling flags and forcing an immediate soft-eviction of pending tiles. Migration notes included in docs/ops/kv-memory-tuning.md.

Risks: - New background scanner uses CPU cycles; defaults tuned conservatively (0.5% CPU budget per node). We measured negligible scheduler interference in staging. - Incorrect priority heuristics could keep cold tiles; mitigated by ephemeral sampling window and eviction fallback heuristics.

Release notes: "Memory: introduce a tessellator that reduces KV cache fragmentation and a spillback smoother that staggers writeback to reduce paging spikes. Feature is disabled by default and can be enabled per-cluster via kv.tessellator_enabled and kv.spill_smoother_enabled. See docs/ops/kv-memory-tuning.md for guidance."

Related work and links: Linear: ENG-4821 (fragmentation investigation), ENG-4890 (paging spike mitigation). Internal perf graphs and fragbench scenarios are attached in the PR (perf/fragbench-2025-10-30/).
notes: Canary to Dedicated clusters for Nov 2025; ops runbook added.
